report.source_text: Chest computed tomography showed emphysematous changes bilaterally with multiple prominent pulmonary bullae bilaterally (blue arrows), the largest in the anterior left upper lobe and posterior right lower lobes (Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3). There were multiple associated regions of bronchiectasis (red arrowheads) and bronchial wall thickening. There was also dilatation of the pulmonary vasculature (red arrows), which should measure <3 cm just proximal to the bifurcation of the left and right pulmonary arteries (Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3).

clinician.final_diagnosis: unique case of COPD bullous emphysema with superimposed pneumonia in a woman of African origin with no hereditary predispositions or social risk factors.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old woman of African origin presented with progressively worsening productive cough, fatigue, shortness of breath, and palpitations. Physical exam revealed respiratory distress, rales, rhonchi, and desaturation on ambulation. A chest CT scan (E001) showed bilateral emphysematous changes with multiple prominent pulmonary bullae, bronchiectasis, bronchial wall thickening, and dilated pulmonary vasculature, consistent with bullous emphysema. Respiratory culture (E003) was positive for Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Candida albicans, leading to broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment, confirming superimposed pneumonia. Pulmonary function tests (E005) revealed FEV1 of 23% and FEV1/FVC ratio of 65%, consistent with severe obstructive lung disease (COPD). Alpha-1 antitrypsin levels (E002) were within normal limits, ruling out a hereditary predisposition.
